editDoReq.how: Edit runs with no link chaos (good/4g/3g/bad, 2-20 parties, both hosts): the room's hibernation events (one per WebSocket frame it is handed) less the hellos, closes and adoption, over the edits committed; read per room from durableObjectsInvocationsAdaptiveGroups by type.

editRowsWritten.how: Same runs: the room's rows written less the adoption's (median of the connect runs) and each connect's, over the edits.

editRowsRead.how: Same runs: the room's rows read over the edits (gross: includes the run's connects and adoption, about 1 row each).

editGBs.how: Same runs: the room's active time (durableObjectsPeriodicGroups activeTime) x 128 MB over the edits, gross (it includes the run's connects: they arrive together, in the same wakes, so a connect run's per-connect figure can't be taken out); a room with hibernatable sockets is billed only while it handles an event.

editRoomCpuMs.how: Same runs: the room's CPU time over the edits (gross).

connWorkerReq.how: 20 connects per run, one at a time, each a real SyncClient that opens, waits until up to date and closes (fresh replica or the same replica reconnecting): the project's requests in wrangler tail over the connects.

connWorkerCpuMs.how: Same runs: the Worker CPU of those requests (wrangler tail cpuTime).

connDoReq.how: Same runs: the room's requests in the connect minutes (they start on a fresh minute after the adoption): the upgrade, the hello, the close.

connRowsWritten.how: Same runs: the room's rows written in the connect minutes over the connects.

connRowsRead.how: Same runs: rows read in the connect minutes over the connects (an empty cut: a long catch-up reads more).

connGBs.how: Same runs: the room's active time in the connect minutes x 128 MB over the connects.

adoptRowsWritten.unit: DO rows written per project adoption
adoptRowsWritten.how: Same runs: the room's rows written in the minutes before the connects (the cut's adoption: 4 tracks, 40 clips).

presenceMsgPerSecWhileDragging.unit: presence frames per second on the wire while dragging
presenceMsgPerSecWhileDragging.how: The Carton web app's PresenceSender fed a drag ghost at 60 Hz (pointermove) for 60 s with 1 and with 4 watchers: frames the transport sent, over 60 s. The sender asks for 20 Hz and SyncClient caps it at PRESENCE_PER_SEC = 10. The Cardboard desktop integration sends at most 1 a second (on pointerdown/keydown/wheel, not while dragging).

presenceDoReq.how: Same runs: the room's hibernation events less every other frame, the adoption and the closes, over the presence frames.

presenceGBs.how: Same runs: the room's active time x 128 MB over the frames, gross (it includes the run's connects and adoption).

presenceRowsWritten.unit: DO rows written per presence frame
presenceRowsWritten.how: Same runs: the room's rows written less the adoption's and the connects', over the frames (presence is never stored).

presenceFanoutPerMsg.unit: frames delivered per presence frame (per watcher)
presenceFanoutPerMsg.how: Same runs: presence events the watchers received over the frames sent, per watcher (outbound frames are not billed).

presenceAlarmPerHour.unit: presence-check alarms per room-hour while someone shows presence
presenceAlarmPerHour.how: One party shows presence once and stays connected, silent but for its keepalive pings, for 15 min (3 rooms at once): the room's alarm invocations in the whole minutes from 90 s after, per hour.

presenceAlarmDoReqPerHour.unit: DO requests per room-hour while someone shows presence (no edits)
presenceAlarmDoReqPerHour.how: Same runs: every request of the room in those minutes, per hour (the alarms; pings are answered by the runtime).

presenceAlarmRowsWritten.unit: DO rows written per presence-check alarm
presenceAlarmRowsWritten.how: Same runs: the room's rows written in those minutes over its alarms.

presenceAlarmGBs.how: Same runs: the room's active time in those minutes x 128 MB over its alarms.

idleDoReqPerHour.unit: DO requests per connected idle party-hour
idleDoReqPerHour.how: 2 and 5 parties connected to one room, nobody editing or showing presence, for 10 min (3 rooms each, at once): the room's requests in the whole minutes from 30 s after all were up, per party-hour.

idleGBsPerHour.unit: DO GB-s per connected idle party-hour
idleGBsPerHour.how: Same runs: the room's active time x 128 MB in those minutes, per party-hour.

idleRowsWrittenPerHour.unit: DO rows written per connected idle party-hour
idleRowsWrittenPerHour.how: Same runs: the room's rows written in those minutes, per party-hour.

gbR2ClassA.unit: R2 Class A operations per GB uploaded
gbR2ClassA.how: 1 GiB uploads with the client's defaults (8 MiB parts, 2 in flight) after fix/cf-stream-parts, unshaped: R2 operations in the upload phase on the project's keys and its uploads' records (r2OperationsAdaptiveGroups by objectName and actionType), Class A per R2's pricing page, per 1e9 bytes. The analytics are sampled (estimates per group, about +/-10% per run); the code path gives 4 per 8 MiB part (UploadPart, and the adapter's lock, record and release objects) + 3 per upload, about 480 per GB.

gbR2ClassB.unit: R2 Class B operations per GB uploaded
gbR2ClassB.how: Same runs: Class B (HeadObject, GetObject) per 1e9 bytes, sampled; the code path gives 1 per part (a head of the upload's meta record) plus the dedup checks, about 120 per GB.

gbWorkerReq.how: Same runs: the project's requests in wrangler tail during the upload phase, per 1e9 bytes.

gbWorkerCpuMs.unit: Worker CPU ms per GB uploaded (R2)
gbWorkerCpuMs.how: Same runs: those requests' CPU time (wrangler tail), per 1e9 bytes.

gbDoReq.unit: DO requests per GB uploaded (R2; the daily write cap's counter)
gbDoReq.how: Same runs: requests to the deployment's write-cap counter room (one reserve per write call) in the upload phase's minutes, per 1e9 bytes; an upper bound (the counter is shared, and other runs' keyframe writes in those minutes count too; the code path gives 1 per part + 2, about 121 per GB); 0 without the cap.

gbVaultRowsWritten.unit: DO rows written per GB uploaded (no R2: the vault)
gbVaultRowsWritten.how: 1 GiB uploads to the no-R2 deployment (blobs in the BlobVault DO), client defaults, unshaped: the project's vault object's rows written in the upload phase, per 1e9 bytes.

gbVaultDoReq.unit: DO requests per GB uploaded (no R2), vault and write cap
gbVaultDoReq.how: Same runs: requests to the vault object and the write-cap counter, per 1e9 bytes.

gbVaultWorkerReq.unit: Worker requests per GB uploaded (no R2)
gbVaultWorkerReq.how: Same runs: the project's requests in wrangler tail during the upload, per 1e9 bytes.

gbVaultWorkerCpuMs.unit: Worker CPU ms per GB uploaded (no R2)
gbVaultWorkerCpuMs.how: Same runs: their CPU time (wrangler tail), per 1e9 bytes.

gbVaultGBs.unit: DO GB-s per GB uploaded (no R2)
gbVaultGBs.how: Same runs: the vault object's active time x 128 MB in the upload phase, per 1e9 bytes.

segWorkerReq.unit: Worker requests per proxy segment published
segWorkerReq.how: not measured yet (1 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. A 10-minute 1280x720 source shared as the app does (shareMedia: libx264 cuts the 720p collab proxy into 2 s CMAF segments, each uploaded as made): the project's requests in wrangler tail over the share, per segment.

segR2ClassA.unit: R2 Class A per proxy segment published
segR2ClassA.how: not measured yet (1 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. Same runs: Class A on the project's keys over the share, per segment.

segR2ClassB.unit: R2 Class B per proxy segment published
segR2ClassB.how: not measured yet (1 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. Same runs: Class B over the share, per segment (dedup checks).

segWorkerCpuMs.unit: Worker CPU ms per proxy segment published
segWorkerCpuMs.how: not measured yet (0 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. Same runs: those requests' CPU (wrangler tail), per segment.

viewWorkerReqPerMiB.how: not measured yet (0 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. A teammate plays the whole proxy from the start as the app's player does (ProxyStreamReader over MediaReader, empty leaf cache): the project's requests in wrangler tail over the play, per MiB.

viewClassBPerMiB.unit: R2 Class B per MiB played
viewClassBPerMiB.how: not measured yet (0 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. Same runs: Class B on the project's keys over the play, per MiB.

viewWorkerCpuMsPerMiB.unit: Worker CPU ms per MiB played
viewWorkerCpuMsPerMiB.how: not measured yet (0 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. Same runs: those requests' CPU (wrangler tail), per MiB.

viewMiBPerGet.unit: MiB per R2 GetObject while playing
viewMiBPerGet.how: not measured yet (0 of 3 runs); costmodel.ts's estimate. Same runs: MiB played over GetObject operations.

editWorkerCpuMs.how: Edits go to the room over the open WebSocket, never through the Worker: in wrangler tail the only Worker requests of a sync run are each connect's upgrade (see connWorkerReq).

limits.observed: Before fix/cf-stream-parts, a part upload read its 8-64 MiB body into JS: 61-359 ms CPU per part; after a burst Cloudflare killed them (exceededCpu, error 1102, HTTP 503). A 1 GB upload to R2 never completed (6 sessions). After the fix a part PUT takes 3-9 ms CPU (256 MB run) and 1 GiB uploads complete in one session (2026-11-02 runs).
limits.carton: Before: a clear HTTP error, 4 retries with backoff, then a resumable stop that never finished. Fixed by streaming the part body to R2 or the vault (fix/cf-stream-parts).

limits.observed: A 96 MiB part failed 503 while another upload shared the isolate; a 99 MiB part alone passed.
limits.carton: Same retry path; streaming parts (fix/cf-stream-parts) no longer buffers them.

limits.value: 100 MB request body (Free and Pro plans)
limits.observed: A 101 MiB part: 413 at the edge; 64, 96 and 99 MiB passed.
limits.carton: Client parts are 8 MiB by default and at most 64 MiB unless a file passes 640 GiB (10,000 parts).

limits.observed: A raw 33 MiB frame: Cloudflare closes 1009; the room closes 1009 above its own 24 MiB cap.
limits.carton: Changes over 1 MiB go as envelopes through blob storage (5 MiB: 2.0-3.5 s, 20 MiB: 3.9-5.1 s, both hosts); a 30 MiB change is refused locally as too large in 215 ms and the next edit still confirms.

limits.value: 1,000 internal subrequests per request (R2 binding calls; Workers Free), 50 external
limits.observed: blobs/heads with 200 keys ok (4.1 s); 1,000 keys answered 200 per call (9.4 s).
limits.carton: The host answers at most BLOB_HEADS_PER_REQUEST keys per call; the client asks again for the rest.

limits.observed: Not hit: the vault stores 1 MiB chunks.

limits.value: not a Cloudflare limit: a dead link keeps the WebSocket 'open'
limits.observed: Old client: through a 5-minute outage the socket stayed open, status 'Syncing' for 5 min, 0 offline events; resumed only on TCP's retransmission timer (everything settled 66.5 s after the edits ended).
limits.carton: Fixed (fix/cf-dead-link): the transport closes a link whose keepalive goes unanswered for 15 s, and pings on a send after silence.

limits.value: not a Cloudflare limit: Workers Free's 100k requests/day across the account
limits.observed: A client whose session the host refuses retried 86 times a minute (~0.57 s gaps), ~2 Worker requests per try: ~245k/day per stuck client, 2.5x the Free plan's daily requests.
limits.carton: Fixed (fix/cf-reconnect-backoff): exponential backoff with jitter to 15 s, 5 min while the session is refused.

limits.value: Workers 100k requests/day; DO 100k requests, 13,000 GB-s, 5M rows read, 100k rows written per day (Free)
limits.observed: Not hit on purpose: hitting one would take the live showcase site down until 00:00 UTC (same account).
limits.carton: Not measured. The lab's own daily write cap (fix/cf-write-cap) was shown instead: 429 DailyWriteCap with Retry-After and a clear message; the uploader stops resumably.

limits.value: the lab deployments' own cap (fix/cf-write-cap): R2 8 GiB/day, no-R2 4 GiB/day, 20k write calls/day
limits.observed: A 256 MB vault upload after the day's earlier uploads was refused: 429 DailyWriteCap.
limits.carton: Refused before any byte is stored; the client backs off and stops resumably with the server's message.

limits.value: not a Cloudflare limit: DO storage 5 GB (Free), $0.20/GB-month (Paid)
limits.observed: The vault had no sweep for abandoned multipart uploads: a killed 1 GB upload left ~600 MB of parts in the DO for good (dropped by the lab).
limits.carton: Fixed on fix/cf-vault-sweep: an alarm deletes unfinished uploads untouched for 24 h.
